name: Frontend development
description: UI framework, design system, responsive, accessibility, theming.

cards.subject: A component
says: is a reusable piece of UI that owns its markup, styling and behaviour
is combined with other components to build pages
cards.use: want to reuse the same card layout on many pages
not: must be a full page of its own

cards.subject: Props
says: pass data from a parent component down to a child
are read-only inside the child that receives them
cards.use: need to give a child component its title and click handler
not: let a child edit the parent's data directly

cards.subject: The children prop
says: lets a parent place arbitrary content inside a wrapper component
makes layout wrappers such as cards and modals reusable
cards.use: build a card whose body differs on every page

cards.subject: A presentational component
says: renders UI purely from the props it receives
has no knowledge of where its data comes from
is easy to test and reuse because it fetches nothing
cards.use: want a button list that can be reused with any data
not: fetches its own data and applies business rules

cards.subject: A container component
says: fetches or prepares data and passes it to presentational children
keeps data loading and business rules out of the visual layer
cards.use: need to load a user's data and hand it to a profile card
not: contains only styling and no logic

cards.subject: A controlled component
says: gets the current value of a form field from state through props
updates that state on every change event
keeps React state as the single source of truth for the input
cards.use: need to validate or reformat input on every keystroke

cards.subject: An uncontrolled component
says: lets the DOM hold the current value of a form field
reads the value through a ref only when needed
cards.use: want a simple form where you read the value once on submit

cards.subject: A list key
says: gives each rendered list item a stable identity
helps the framework match items between renders
should not be the array index when items can be reordered
cards.use: render a list of rows that users can sort and delete
not: must be unique across the whole page

cards.subject: An error boundary
says: catches errors thrown while rendering its children
shows a fallback UI instead of a blank page
does not catch errors inside event handlers
cards.use: want one broken widget not to take down the whole page
not: catches every error including those in async code and handlers

cards.subject: Compound components
says: share implicit state between a parent and its related children
let you write Tabs with Tabs.List and Tabs.Panel pieces
give consumers flexible composition instead of a long props list
cards.use: build a tabs widget whose pieces consumers arrange freely

cards.subject: A server component
says: renders on the server and sends no component code to the browser
can read data directly on the server
cannot use browser-only features such as click handlers or local state
cards.use: want a page section that only displays data and needs no interactivity
not: can attach an onClick handler

cards.subject: A client component
says: is marked with the use client directive
runs in the browser and can hold state and handle events
adds its code to the JavaScript bundle sent to users
cards.use: need a form with local state and click handlers
not: is rendered only once on the server and never in the browser

cards.subject: A design system
says: is a shared set of rules, tokens and components with usage guidance
makes products consistent and speeds up design and development
cards.use: want designers and developers to stop reinventing buttons

cards.subject: A design token
says: is a named value such as a colour, spacing step or corner radius
lets one change update every component that uses it
cards.use: want to change the brand colour in one place
not: is a login credential for the design tool

cards.subject: A semantic token
says: is named by purpose such as surface or text-muted
can point to a different value in each theme
cards.use: need a muted text colour that works in both light and dark themes
not: is named after its colour such as light-grey

cards.subject: A primitive token
says: holds a raw value such as a specific shade of blue
sits underneath semantic tokens as the base palette
cards.use: need the raw palette that semantic tokens map onto

cards.subject: A spacing scale
says: limits margins and padding to a small set of steps
keeps gaps consistent across screens
cards.use: want gaps to look consistent without arguing about pixels

cards.subject: Theming
says: swaps token values to change the look without changing components
supports variants such as light, dark or a partner brand
cards.use: need the same components to carry a second brand

cards.subject: Dark mode
says: is the same components with a second set of token values
can follow the operating system preference or a user switch
cards.use: want the interface to follow the user's system appearance setting
not: needs a separate copy of every component

cards.subject: A CSS custom property
says: holds a value declared with a double dash name and read with var()
can be overridden for a subtree or a theme at runtime
cards.use: want to change a colour by switching a class on the page root

cards.subject: Design drift
says: happens when product screens slowly diverge from the design system
is reduced by regular reviews and by removing unused parts
cards.use: find three slightly different blues across the product

cards.subject: Mobile-first design
says: starts with the small-screen layout and adds rules as space grows
usually writes min-width media queries
cards.use: want the phone experience to be the baseline

cards.subject: A media query
says: applies CSS only when a condition such as viewport width is met
can also test preferences such as reduced motion or colour scheme
cards.use: want a different layout on wide screens

cards.subject: A breakpoint
says: is the width at which the layout changes
should be chosen where the content starts to break, not by device name
cards.use: see a sidebar squash the text at tablet width

cards.subject: The viewport meta tag
says: tells mobile browsers to match the layout width to the device width
is needed for media queries to behave properly on phones
cards.use: find that a mobile page shows as a tiny zoomed-out desktop layout

cards.subject: Flexbox
says: lays items out along one axis, in a row or a column
distributes free space and aligns items within a single line or wrap
cards.use: need a toolbar whose items sit in a row and share space
not: places items in rows and columns at once by default

cards.subject: CSS Grid
says: lays items out in rows and columns at the same time
lets items span several tracks
cards.use: need a dashboard with named areas across rows and columns

cards.subject: Relative units
says: size things such as text and spacing from a root or parent value
let layouts respect the user's chosen font size
cards.use: want text to scale when the user raises the browser font size
not: are fixed pixel sizes

cards.subject: Responsive images
says: offer several image sizes through srcset and sizes
let the browser pick a file that fits the screen
cards.use: want phones to avoid downloading a desktop-sized hero photo

cards.subject: A container query
says: styles a component based on the size of its container
lets one card adapt differently in a sidebar and in a wide column
cards.use: need a card that adapts to the space it is placed in rather than the screen

cards.subject: Fluid typography
says: scales text smoothly between a minimum and maximum size
is commonly written with the clamp() function
cards.use: want headings to grow gradually with the viewport instead of in jumps

cards.subject: WCAG
says: is the W3C standard of testable accessibility success criteria
has conformance levels A, AA and AAA
is organised around being perceivable, operable, understandable and robust
cards.use: need a standard to measure accessibility against

cards.subject: Semantic HTML
says: uses elements such as button, nav and h1 for their meaning
gives assistive technology roles and keyboard behaviour for free
cards.use: want a clickable control that works with a keyboard without extra code
not: is only for search engines and has no accessibility value

cards.subject: Alternative text
says: gives a text equivalent of a meaningful image
should be empty for purely decorative images
cards.use: add a chart image that carries information

cards.subject: Keyboard navigation
says: lets users reach and operate every control without a mouse
follows an order that matches the visual reading order
cards.use: have users who cannot use a pointing device

cards.subject: A focus indicator
says: shows which element currently has keyboard focus
must not be removed unless replaced by something equally visible
cards.use: see designers asking to remove the outline because it looks ugly

cards.subject: Colour contrast
says: compares the lightness of text against its background
requires at least 4.5 to 1 for normal text at level AA
cards.use: check that grey text is readable on a white card
not: is satisfied by any colour pair that looks pleasant

cards.subject: A form label
says: is programmatically tied to its input
gives the field an accessible name and a bigger click area
cards.use: find that a screen reader says only edit text for a field
not: can be replaced by placeholder text alone

cards.subject: ARIA
says: adds roles, states and properties to improve the accessibility tree
should be used only when no native element does the job
does not add keyboard behaviour by itself
cards.use: build a custom widget with no native HTML equivalent
not: makes a div behave like a button in every way once the role is added

cards.subject: An aria-label
says: gives an element an accessible name that is not visible text
is typical for an icon-only button
cards.use: have a button showing only a magnifier icon

cards.subject: A skip link
says: lets keyboard users jump past repeated navigation to the main content
is usually the first focusable element on the page
cards.use: see keyboard users tabbing through forty menu links on every page

cards.subject: A reduced motion preference
says: is a user setting that asks for less animation
is read with the prefers-reduced-motion media query
cards.use: want to tone down parallax or confetti for users who get dizzy

cards.subject: A live region
says: announces dynamic changes to a screen reader without moving focus
is created with aria-live or roles such as status and alert
cards.use: show a toast saying the save succeeded

cards.subject: A focus trap
says: keeps keyboard focus inside an open modal dialog
returns focus to the opener when the dialog closes
cards.use: open a modal where Tab must not reach the page behind

cards.subject: A positive tabindex
says: forces an element earlier in the tab order than natural order
is usually avoided because it makes order hard to maintain
cards.use: are tempted to reorder tab stops with numbers greater than zero

cards.subject: Core Web Vitals
says: are Google's user-centred metrics for loading, responsiveness and visual stability
are measured on real users in the field and in lab tools
cards.use: need a shared set of metrics for page experience

cards.subject: Largest Contentful Paint
says: measures how long the largest visible content element takes to render
is often a hero image or a main heading
cards.use: want to know how fast the main content appears
not: measures layout movement after load

cards.subject: Cumulative Layout Shift
says: measures unexpected movement of visible content
is reduced by reserving space for images and ads
cards.use: see a button jump as an image finishes loading

cards.subject: Interaction to Next Paint
says: measures how quickly the page responds visually to user input
gets worse when long tasks block the main thread
cards.use: find that clicks feel sluggish on a busy page

cards.subject: Bundle size
says: is the amount of JavaScript and CSS users must download
grows with every dependency you add
cards.use: see that a date library doubled the download size

cards.subject: Code splitting
says: breaks the bundle into chunks loaded when needed
is usually done at route or dynamic import boundaries
cards.use: want the admin screens not to slow the home page

cards.subject: Lazy loading
says: delays loading images or components until they are about to be needed
is enabled for images with the loading attribute set to lazy
cards.use: have a long page with many images far below the fold
not: should be applied to the main hero image

cards.subject: Tree shaking
says: removes unused exports from the final bundle
works best with ES module imports
cards.use: import one function from a large utility library
not: removes unused CSS from the page by itself

cards.subject: Image optimisation
says: uses modern formats, right sizes and compression
gives width and height so the browser can reserve space
cards.use: need the page images to weigh less

cards.subject: A CDN
says: serves static assets from locations close to users
lowers latency and offloads traffic from the origin
cards.use: serve users in many countries with the same files

cards.subject: Cache-Control
says: is an HTTP header that tells browsers and caches how long to keep a response
allows fingerprinted assets to be cached for a long time
cards.use: need hashed bundles to be reused across visits

cards.subject: A render-blocking resource
says: delays first paint until it has downloaded and been processed
is typically CSS in the head or a synchronous script
cards.use: see a blank screen while a big script loads

cards.subject: Debouncing
says: waits until activity stops before running a function
avoids firing a search request on every keystroke
cards.use: want to call the search API only after typing pauses

cards.subject: List virtualization
says: renders only the rows currently visible in the viewport
keeps the DOM small for lists with thousands of items
cards.use: need to show a table with fifty thousand rows

cards.subject: A performance budget
says: sets a limit for bundle size or a metric that builds must respect
can fail the pipeline when a limit is exceeded
cards.use: want to stop the app silently getting heavier each sprint

cards.subject: Real user monitoring
says: collects performance data from actual visitors
reveals slow devices and networks lab tests miss
cards.use: see good lab scores but complaints from users in slow regions

cards.subject: A preload hint
says: tells the browser to fetch a critical resource early
is suited to the hero image or a font used on first paint
cards.use: know that the largest image is discovered late by the browser

cards.subject: Local state
says: belongs to one component and lives only while it is mounted
suits things such as an open dropdown or an input draft
cards.use: track whether a menu is open

cards.subject: Lifting state up
says: moves shared state to the nearest common parent
lets sibling components stay in sync
cards.use: need two sibling components to show the same selection

cards.subject: Global state
says: is available to many distant components through a store or context
is easy to overuse for data only one screen needs
cards.use: need the signed-in user in the header and on many pages

cards.subject: Prop drilling
says: passes props through many layers that do not use them
makes refactoring harder as the tree grows
cards.use: see a theme value handed through five wrapper components

cards.subject: Server state
says: is data owned by the backend and cached in the client
needs handling for loading, errors and staleness
cards.use: show a list of records fetched from an API

cards.subject: URL state
says: stores filters, sorting or a page number in the address
makes a view linkable, bookmarkable and shareable
cards.use: want a filtered list to survive a refresh and be sent to a colleague

cards.subject: Derived state
says: is computed from existing state instead of being stored again
avoids copies that fall out of sync
cards.use: need the total price of items already in a cart

cards.subject: A reducer
says: computes the next state from the current state and an action
centralises state transitions in one testable function
cards.use: have many related updates that must follow strict rules

cards.subject: An optimistic update
says: shows the expected result before the server confirms
rolls back if the request fails
cards.use: want a like button to feel instant

cards.subject: Cache invalidation of fetched data
says: marks cached server data as stale after a change
triggers a refetch so the screen shows current values
cards.use: see old data after saving an edit on another screen

cards.subject: Client-side validation
says: runs checks in the browser before the request is sent
is a convenience that a user can bypass
cards.use: want a friendly message for an empty email field
not: makes server checks unnecessary

cards.subject: Server-side validation
says: checks every submitted value again on the server
is the authority that cannot be bypassed by editing the page
cards.use: must trust only what an attacker cannot change

cards.subject: An inline error message
says: appears next to the field that failed
explains the problem in plain words
cards.use: want users to see which field is wrong and why

cards.subject: Double-submit protection
says: disables the submit button or ignores repeats while a request is in flight
prevents duplicate orders or records
cards.use: find users clicking Pay twice on a slow connection

cards.subject: The autocomplete attribute
says: tells the browser what kind of value a field expects
lets browsers and password managers fill the field accurately
cards.use: want address and email fields to fill automatically

cards.subject: The accept attribute on a file input
says: filters the file picker by type
is only a hint and does not enforce anything
cards.use: want the picker to show only images
not: guarantees that every uploaded file is an image

cards.subject: A content-based file type check
says: inspects the file bytes to identify the real format
does not trust the extension or the declared type
cards.use: must be sure an uploaded file is truly a PNG
not: trusts the file name ending

cards.subject: An idempotency key
says: is a unique value sent with a request so a repeat is processed once
lets a retry after a timeout avoid creating a duplicate
cards.use: must retry a payment request safely after a network failure

cards.subject: Client-side rendering
says: builds the page in the browser from JavaScript
shows little useful HTML until the script runs
cards.use: build a logged-in dashboard where SEO does not matter
not: delivers complete HTML for crawlers on first response

cards.subject: Server-side rendering
says: generates HTML on the server for each request
sends content users and crawlers see right away
cards.use: need fresh, personalised content that crawlers can read

cards.subject: Static site generation
says: builds pages to HTML once at build time
serves pre-built pages cheaply from a CDN
cards.use: have a marketing page that changes rarely
not: renders again on every request

cards.subject: Client-side routing
says: swaps views in the browser without a full page reload
keeps the shell loaded between navigations
cards.use: want fast navigation between screens of an app

cards.subject: Hydration
says: attaches event handlers to HTML that the server already rendered
makes server-rendered markup interactive
cards.use: see a server-rendered button that does nothing until scripts load

cards.subject: A hydration mismatch
says: happens when server HTML differs from the first client render
is often caused by values such as the current time or random numbers
cards.use: see a warning after rendering a timestamp on the server

cards.subject: Incremental static regeneration
says: rebuilds a static page in the background after a set interval
serves the old page until the new one is ready
cards.use: want mostly static pages that refresh every few minutes

cards.subject: Streaming rendering
says: sends parts of the page as they become ready
lets slow sections show a fallback while fast ones appear
cards.use: have one slow data call blocking an otherwise fast page

cards.subject: Partial hydration
says: hydrates only the interactive parts of a page
ships less JavaScript for mostly static content
cards.use: want a content page with a couple of interactive widgets

cards.subject: A progressive web app
says: is a website that can be installed and work with poor connectivity
combines HTTPS, a manifest and a service worker
cards.use: want a web app that can be added to the home screen

cards.subject: A service worker
says: is a script that runs separately from the page and intercepts network requests
enables offline support and caching strategies
is registered by the page through navigator.serviceWorker.register
cards.use: need the app to open without a network
not: can read and change the page DOM directly

cards.subject: A web app manifest
says: is a JSON file with the app's name, icons and display mode
makes a site installable
cards.use: want a custom icon and standalone window when installed

cards.subject: Progressive enhancement
says: starts from working HTML and layers features on top
keeps core content usable when scripts fail
cards.use: want the basic task to work on any browser

cards.subject: Graceful degradation
says: builds the full experience first and plans a fallback
reduces features when something is unsupported
cards.use: must keep an advanced design usable in an old browser

cards.subject: Feature detection
says: tests whether a capability exists before using it
is preferred over guessing from the browser name
cards.use: want to use an API only where it is supported
not: reads the user agent string to identify the browser

cards.subject: A polyfill
says: adds a missing browser feature using JavaScript
should be loaded only for browsers that need it
cards.use: need a newer API on an older browser

cards.subject: A stale-while-revalidate strategy
says: serves a cached copy immediately and refreshes it in the background
balances speed with freshness
cards.use: want a quick response but updated data next time

cards.subject: A cache-first strategy
says: answers from the cache and goes to the network only on a miss
suits versioned static assets
cards.use: serve fingerprinted files that never change

cards.subject: A browserslist target
says: declares which browsers the build must support
drives how much code is transpiled and polyfilled
cards.use: want to decide how far back to support old browsers

cards.subject: Linting
says: flags suspicious code and style problems without running it
can enforce accessibility rules in JSX
cards.use: want to catch unused variables before review

cards.subject: A unit test
says: checks a small piece such as a function or component in isolation
runs fast and pinpoints a failure
cards.use: verify a price formatting function

cards.subject: Type checking
says: catches wrong data shapes and calls before the code runs
documents what components accept
cards.use: want a mistyped prop name caught while coding

cards.subject: A component test
says: renders one component and checks what the user would see
interacts through clicks and typing
cards.use: verify a form shows an error after a bad submit

cards.subject: An end-to-end test
says: drives a real browser through a whole user journey
is slower and more fragile than unit tests
cards.use: verify that a user can sign in and finish a purchase

cards.subject: Testing by accessible role
says: finds elements the way users and assistive technology do
fails when markup loses its semantics
cards.use: want tests that do not break on class name changes
not: relies on generated CSS class names

cards.subject: Network mocking
says: replaces real API calls with controlled responses
makes tests fast and repeatable
cards.use: need a test to see a server error without a real server

cards.subject: An automated accessibility check
says: scans a page for detectable issues such as missing labels
finds only part of the real problems
cards.use: want every pull request scanned for obvious accessibility errors
not: proves a page is fully accessible

cards.subject: A visual regression test
says: compares screenshots against an approved baseline
flags unintended layout or style changes
cards.use: worry that a CSS change broke some other screen

cards.subject: A flaky test
says: passes and fails without a code change
erodes trust in the suite until fixed or removed
cards.use: see a test failing on every tenth run

cards.subject: Cross-site scripting
says: injects attacker script into a page that other users view
can steal sessions or act as the victim
cards.use: find that a comment field shows script tags as live code

cards.subject: Output encoding
says: turns special characters into harmless text before display
is the main defence against injection into HTML
cards.use: must show user-supplied names inside a page safely

cards.subject: dangerouslySetInnerHTML
says: inserts raw HTML strings into the DOM in React
bypasses automatic escaping, so input must be sanitised
cards.use: are tempted to render rich text from a user
not: escapes the content for you

cards.subject: A Content Security Policy
says: is a response header that limits where scripts and other resources may load from
reduces the damage from injected script
cards.use: want a second layer of defence against XSS
not: replaces output encoding

cards.subject: Cross-site request forgery
says: tricks a logged-in browser into sending an unwanted request
is countered by anti-forgery tokens and by restricting cross-site cookies
cards.use: worry that another site can submit a form as the user

cards.subject: An HttpOnly cookie
says: cannot be read by JavaScript
limits what an XSS attack can steal
cards.use: store a session identifier safely

cards.subject: A SameSite cookie
says: is not sent on most cross-site requests
is set with the SameSite attribute using Lax or Strict
cards.use: want to limit cookies sent from other sites

cards.subject: CORS
says: lets a server say which other origins may read its responses in browsers
is enforced by the browser, not the server
cards.use: see a browser block a call to another domain's API
not: protects the server from non-browser clients

cards.subject: Subresource Integrity
says: checks a hash of a third-party file before running it
blocks a script that was tampered with on a CDN
cards.use: load a library from a CDN you do not control

cards.subject: Secrets in client code
says: are visible to anyone who opens the browser tools
must therefore stay on the server
cards.use: are about to put a private API key into a front-end variable
not: are safe if the variable name is hard to guess

cards.subject: The title tag
says: names the page in search results and browser tabs
should be unique for each page
cards.use: want each page to have a clear name in search

cards.subject: A meta description
says: summarises the page for the search result snippet
does not directly raise rankings
cards.use: want to control the text under a search result

cards.subject: Heading structure
says: uses one clear h1 and ordered subheadings
helps both crawlers and screen readers understand the outline
cards.use: find a page that skips from h1 to h5 for styling

cards.subject: A sitemap
says: lists the URLs you want crawlers to find
helps discovery of pages with few inbound links
cards.use: launch a large site with deep pages

cards.subject: The robots.txt file
says: asks crawlers not to fetch certain paths
does not hide a page that other sites link to
cards.use: want crawlers to skip an internal search results area

cards.subject: A canonical URL
says: names the preferred address among duplicate pages
consolidates ranking signals onto one URL
cards.use: have the same page reachable with several query strings

cards.subject: Open Graph tags
says: control the title and image when a link is shared on social platforms
are placed in the page head
cards.use: want a good preview when a link is pasted into chat

cards.subject: A noindex directive
says: asks search engines to keep a page out of results
must stay crawlable to be seen
cards.use: have a thank-you page that should not be searchable

cards.subject: Structured data
says: describes page content in a machine-readable vocabulary
can make results eligible for rich snippets
cards.use: want a recipe or product to show extra detail in search

cards.subject: The gglearn web stack
says: uses Next.js, which is built on React
is shared with the company's other web apps
cards.use: need to know which framework the gglearn screens are built with

cards.subject: The gglearn components folder
says: holds the visuals such as avatars, rank shields, race track, score rings and confetti
contains no image assets
cards.use: look for where gglearn's drawn visuals live

cards.subject: gglearn avatars and rank shields
says: are drawn as SVG components rather than image files
stay tiny and scale to any screen
cards.use: wonder why gglearn needs no downloaded pictures for ranks

cards.subject: gglearn confetti
says: is a celebration animation that should respect the reduced motion setting
is drawn in the components folder
cards.use: want to calm gglearn's celebration for motion-sensitive users

cards.subject: The gglearn bot label
says: names bots in words as Bot and simulated on the competitions leaderboard
avoids relying on colour alone to show who is a bot
cards.use: wonder why a leaderboard row says Bot instead of only using a different colour

cards.subject: The gglearn photo format rule
says: allows JPEG, PNG or WebP for profile photos
rejects other formats
cards.use: need to know what a user may upload as a profile photo

cards.subject: The gglearn photo size limit
says: caps a profile photo at 300 KB
applies to every JPEG, PNG or WebP profile photo
cards.use: need the biggest profile photo gglearn accepts

cards.subject: The gglearn photo type check
says: identifies the format from the file bytes
ignores what the file name says
cards.use: want to see how gglearn decides an upload is really a JPEG, PNG or WebP

cards.subject: The gglearn SVG upload ban
says: rejects SVG uploads because SVG can carry scripts
is part of the profile photo checks
cards.use: wonder why a vector file cannot be a gglearn profile photo

cards.subject: The gglearn upload checks location
says: run on the server and not only in the screen
cannot be skipped by editing the page
cards.use: ask where gglearn enforces its photo rules

cards.subject: The gglearn Next.js docs rule
says: says to read the bundled docs in node_modules/next/dist/docs before coding
exists because this Next.js version has breaking changes
cards.use: are about to write a Next.js API from memory

cards.subject: The framework choice rule
says: says to choose a framework for team fit and longevity
warns against choosing by novelty
cards.use: are asked how the company picks a UI framework

qa.q: Which HTML element should you use for a control that performs an action when clicked?
qa.right: button
qa.why: A native button brings keyboard activation and semantics for free.

qa.q: What does this tag do?
qa.right: It tells mobile browsers to match the layout width to the device width
wrong: It disables zooming on every device
It forces desktop layout on phones
qa.why: The viewport meta tag controls the layout viewport on mobile.

qa.q: What is the purpose of alt text on a meaningful image?
qa.right: To give screen reader users a text equivalent
wrong: To make the image load faster
To set the image tooltip colour
To improve rendering in old printers
qa.why: Alt text is the accessible text alternative.

qa.q: Why does a browser-side check not replace a server check?
qa.right: Users can bypass the browser and send requests directly
wrong: Servers cannot receive form data without it
It is slower than the server check
qa.why: Only server checks are authoritative.

qa.q: What does this CSS rule express?
qa.right: Apply the style from 600px wide upward
wrong: Apply the style only on printers
qa.why: A min-width query is the mobile-first pattern.

qa.q: Which statement about design tokens is correct?
qa.right: They are named values such as colours and spacing reused by components
wrong: They are secret keys for the design tool
They are cookies set by the browser
They are paid licences for fonts
qa.why: Tokens are the base layer of a design system.

qa.q: What does this code render?
qa.right: The text from the title variable, escaped as plain text
wrong: The title as raw HTML markup
Only the first character of the title
qa.why: JSX escapes text interpolated in braces.

qa.q: What is wrong with this input?
qa.right: It has no associated label for assistive technology
wrong: It uses the wrong input type
It cannot be focused with the keyboard
qa.why: A placeholder is not a label.

qa.q: What does this attribute do for a below-the-fold image?
qa.right: Delays loading until the image is near the viewport
wrong: Converts it to a smaller format
qa.why: The loading lazy attribute defers offscreen images.

qa.q: Which colour contrast ratio is the minimum for normal text at level AA?
qa.why: AA asks for 4.5:1, with 3:1 for large text.

qa.q: What is the benefit of giving an img width and height attributes?
qa.right: The browser can reserve space and avoid layout shift
wrong: The server resizes it on request
qa.why: Reserved space reduces Cumulative Layout Shift.

qa.q: Where does data fetched for a read-only page section best live in a framework with server components?
qa.right: In a server component that renders it
wrong: In a client component with a global store
In a cookie on every request
qa.why: Server components keep code and data access off the client.

qa.q: What does the prefers-color-scheme media query detect?
qa.right: The operating system light or dark preference
qa.why: It lets CSS follow the user's setting.

qa.q: Why is the key prop given to list items?
qa.right: It lets the framework match items between renders
wrong: It sets the item's CSS class
qa.why: Stable keys avoid wrong reuse of rows.

qa.q: What does this snippet do for users who ask for less motion?
qa.right: It disables the animation for them
qa.why: The query matches the reduced motion setting.

qa.q: What is the problem with this code?
qa.right: Using the array index as key breaks identity when rows are reordered
wrong: The map call cannot return elements
The li element cannot hold text
The items variable must be a string
qa.why: Index keys cause state to attach to the wrong row.

qa.q: What does a useEffect with an empty dependency array do?
qa.right: It runs once after the first render
wrong: It runs before the first render
qa.why: An empty array means no dependencies change.

qa.q: What is the risk in this code?
qa.right: If html contains user input, it can run script and enable XSS
wrong: It only works on the server
qa.why: Raw HTML insertion skips escaping.

qa.q: Which role does aria-label serve in this markup?
qa.right: It gives the icon-only button an accessible name
wrong: It makes the button keyboard focusable
qa.why: Without it, a screen reader has nothing to read.

qa.q: Which header would you set to reduce damage from injected scripts by limiting script sources?
qa.right: Content-Security-Policy
qa.why: CSP restricts where scripts may load from.

qa.q: Why are long-lived Cache-Control headers safe on hashed bundle files?
qa.right: The file name changes whenever the content changes
wrong: Browsers ignore the header for scripts
The server deletes old files hourly
qa.why: A new hash gives a new URL.

qa.q: What does this code do on user input?
qa.right: It waits until typing pauses before calling search
wrong: It calls search on every keystroke
qa.why: This is debouncing.

qa.q: Which metric measures unexpected movement of content while the page loads?
qa.right: Cumulative Layout Shift
qa.why: CLS measures visual stability.

qa.q: What does a dynamic import enable?
qa.right: Loading a chunk only when it is needed
wrong: Running code on the server only
qa.why: Dynamic import is the code splitting boundary.

qa.q: Which file type check is the safest for an upload on the server?
qa.right: Inspect the file bytes to identify the format
wrong: Trust the declared content type header
Trust the accept attribute on the input
qa.why: Names and headers are supplied by the client.

qa.q: What does the accept attribute on a file input guarantee?
qa.right: Nothing; it only filters the file picker
wrong: That the server will refuse other types
That the file is under a size limit
qa.why: It is a hint, so validate on the server.

qa.q: Why does gglearn reject SVG profile photos?
qa.right: SVG can carry scripts
wrong: SVG files are always larger than 300 KB
SVG cannot be displayed in browsers
qa.why: The company source gives this reason: an SVG can include script.

qa.q: What is the maximum profile photo size in gglearn?
qa.right: 300 KB
qa.why: The size limit comes from the competitions document.

qa.q: Which formats does gglearn accept for profile photos?
qa.right: JPEG, PNG or WebP
qa.why: These are the allowed types.

qa.q: What does gglearn use to draw avatars and rank shields?
qa.right: SVG components
qa.why: The README says visuals are drawn without image assets.

qa.q: A Next.js team member writes API code from memory. What does the gglearn project instruct?
qa.right: Read the bundled docs first
wrong: Pin the version and never read docs
qa.why: The project says this version has breaking changes.

qa.q: Which test finds elements the way a user would?
qa.right: Query by accessible role and name
wrong: Query by position in the DOM tree
qa.why: Role queries survive restyling and verify semantics.

qa.q: A team removes the focus outline because designers dislike it. What should they do?
qa.right: Replace it with a clear custom focus style
wrong: Leave nothing, since users have mice
Make focus invisible but keep tab order
qa.why: Keyboard users need a visible indicator.

qa.q: A page scores well in lab tests, but field data shows poor responsiveness on cheap phones. What is the best first step?
qa.right: Profile long tasks and reduce JavaScript on the main thread
wrong: Add more images to the hero
qa.why: Slow devices expose main thread cost.

qa.q: A product page needs fresh prices on every request and good SEO. Which rendering is the best fit?
qa.right: Server-side rendering
wrong: Static generation at build with no refresh
qa.why: SSR sends current HTML to crawlers.

qa.q: A blog's pages change a few times a day and must be fast and cheap to serve. What fits?
qa.right: Static generation with periodic regeneration
wrong: Rendering on every request with no caching
qa.why: Regeneration keeps pages static but fresh.

qa.q: A server-rendered page logs a hydration mismatch after printing the current time. What is the likely cause?
qa.right: The server and the client render different times
wrong: The CSS file is too large
The images have no alt text
qa.why: Values that vary between renders must be handled after mount.

qa.q: A modal opens, but pressing Tab moves focus to the page behind it. What is missing?
qa.right: A focus trap
qa.why: Modals must keep focus inside until closed.

qa.q: A team puts an API key in a front-end environment variable exposed to the browser. What is the problem?
qa.right: Anyone can read it in the bundle or network tools
qa.why: Secrets must live on the server.

qa.q: A designer asks for a new almost-blue for one screen. What does a healthy design system process do?
qa.right: Check whether an existing token fits, and add one only for a real need
wrong: Add a new hex value inline
qa.why: This prevents design drift.

qa.q: A like button waits for the server before changing. Users say it feels slow. What can improve it?
qa.right: An optimistic update with rollback on failure
qa.why: Show the expected state immediately and reconcile.

qa.q: A search page calls the API on each keystroke and shows results out of order. What is the best fix?
qa.right: Debounce input and ignore stale responses
qa.why: Debouncing plus cancellation avoids races.

qa.q: A long product list of 20,000 rows freezes the browser. What helps most?
qa.right: List virtualization
qa.why: Rendering only visible rows keeps the DOM small.

qa.q: A team wants a custom dropdown with div elements. What is the best approach?
qa.right: Use a native select unless a custom widget is truly needed, then follow ARIA patterns
wrong: Add role button to every div and stop
Use colour alone for the selected item
qa.why: Native elements first, ARIA when needed.

qa.q: A pull request adds a 200 KB date library for one format call. What do you ask?
qa.right: Whether a smaller alternative or native API will do
wrong: Whether it has a nice logo
Whether it can be placed in the head
Whether the bundle can be ignored
qa.why: Dependencies cost bundle size.

qa.q: The leaderboard shows bots only by a grey colour. What accessibility change fits gglearn's own approach?
qa.right: Label them in words as Bot
wrong: Add a tooltip only for mouse users
qa.why: Do not use colour alone to carry meaning.

qa.q: A user's long form fails on the server and the fields clear. What should happen?
qa.right: Keep what they typed and show errors by the fields
wrong: Clear the form to be safe
Show one alert and nothing else
qa.why: Forgiving forms retain input.

qa.q: A team adds tabindex values 1, 2, 3 to force a tab order. What is the issue?
qa.right: Positive tabindex breaks natural order and is hard to maintain
qa.why: Fix DOM order instead.

qa.q: A payment request times out and the client retries. What prevents a double charge?
qa.right: An idempotency key on the request
wrong: A disabled button after the retry
qa.why: The server processes a repeated key once.

qa.q: A page loads a library from a CDN. What protects against a tampered file?
qa.right: Subresource Integrity
qa.why: SRI verifies a hash of the file.

qa.q: A content page needs two interactive widgets and little else. Which approach minimises shipped JavaScript?
qa.right: Partial hydration or isolating client components
wrong: Bundling all widgets on every route
qa.why: Hydrating only what is interactive saves JavaScript.

qa.q: A report says all automated accessibility checks passed. What is the sensible conclusion?
qa.right: Manual keyboard and screen reader testing is still required
wrong: No further testing is needed ever
qa.why: Automation finds only part of the issues.

qa.q: A security review finds script injected through a comment. Which pair gives the best defence in depth?
qa.right: Output encoding plus a Content Security Policy
wrong: A larger font plus a sitemap
qa.why: Encoding prevents injection, CSP limits damage.

qa.q: A service worker caches the HTML shell forever and users never see new releases. What should change?
qa.right: Version the cache and use a revalidating strategy for the shell
qa.why: Stale shells need an update path.

qa.q: A team sets a rule that fails the build when the main bundle exceeds a limit. What is this?
qa.right: A performance budget
qa.why: Budgets turn performance into a gate.
